# Contributing

Thanks for helping improve our engineering standards.

This repo holds the standards in plain language. Per-repo tooling is configured to match
what lives here, so a change to a standard can ripple out to every repo that follows it.
That makes thoughtful, well-reasoned changes worth the effort.

## Proposing a change

- Keep each pull request focused on a single standard or idea. Small, clear changes are
  easier to agree on.
- Explain the why. A standard is easier to adopt when the reasoning is written down.
- Point to real examples where you can. A standard grounded in code we actually write is
  stronger than one argued in the abstract.
- Write for a human first. These pages are read by people and by AI agents, so keep the
  language clear and the scope of each page tight.

## What belongs here

- Conventions worth stating in plain language: naming, structure, testing, idioms, and the
  principles behind them.
- Guidance that tools cannot fully capture on their own, or that should shape the tooling
  we add per repo.

## What does not

- Repo-specific rules. Those live in the repo they apply to.
- Exhaustive mechanical formatting that a formatter already handles.
